problem: Suppose $B$ is a $6\times 6$ matrix and $det(B)=200.$ The matrix $C$ is obtained from $B$ by applying the elementary row operation ${R}_{6}:=\frac{3}{50}{R}_{6}.$ What is the value of $det(C)?$
worked_solution:
The row operation applied to $B$ consists of multiplying a row by the number $\frac{3}{50}.$

When we do this, the determinant is multiplied by the same number. So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}det(C) & =\frac{3}{50}det(B) \\  & =\frac{3}{50}\cdot 200 \\  & =12.\end{aligned}
$$
